category_title: Grade 6 student with behavioral exceptionalities and migration-related learning difficulties
student_description: Dwayne is a Grade 6 student who struggles with independent work, emotional regulation, and peer interactions, often presenting as loud, controlling, or easily frustrated. His history of segregation has led to a learned helplessness where he relies heavily on constant adult presence. He uniquely requires explicit workload reductions, strengths-based feedback on poor grades, and non-punitive behavioral mirroring to build self-awareness and confidence without triggering defiance.

criteria.rationale: Dwayne lacks the confidence to tackle standard assignments and will refuse to work if he feels overwhelmed.
criteria.check: The tutor explicitly reduces the quantity, length, or scope of the immediate task to make it feel more manageable for the student.

criteria.rationale: Dwayne is prone to sudden temper outbursts and needs concrete, physical strategies to self-regulate before escalating.
criteria.check: The tutor provides a specific, actionable physical out (such as walking away or getting a drink of water) when the student shows signs of anger or frustration.

criteria.rationale: Dwayne is often unaware of his loud, obnoxious behavior and responds better to behavioral mirroring than to punitive scolding.
criteria.check: The tutor matches the student's volume or energy level to demonstrate his behavior, prompting him to recognize his own loudness without direct reprimand.

criteria.rationale: Dwayne is easily defeated by poor grades and will reject the work entirely if he feels he has failed.
criteria.check: The tutor explicitly highlights a specific positive element or something the student did well, even when delivering a poor grade or correcting mistakes.

criteria.rationale: Dwayne has been socialized to rely on constant 1:1 support and will not develop independence if the tutor does the work for him.
criteria.check: The tutor avoids doing the task for the student or hovering constantly, instead setting an expectation for him to attempt a portion independently.
